questions.q: What is the meaning of Embroidery?
options: The process of carving wood using a sharp chisel.
The craft of decorating fabric or other materials using a needle and thread or yarn.
The method of folding paper to make animal shapes.
The application of wet wax on fabric.
questions.explain: Embroidery is a textile craft that involves using a needle to apply yarn or thread in various stitches to create decorative designs on the surface of a fabric.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which of the following describes the 'Herringbone' stitch used in embroidery?
options: A continuous chain of interlinked loops.
A flat stitch that looks like a row of small pearls.
A crossed, zig-zag stitch resembling the bones of a fish.
questions.explain: The herringbone stitch produces a decorative crossed zig-zag pattern that mimics the skeleton of a herring fish. It is often used for borders and catching hems.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: The embroidery stitch that creates a textured, rope-like line, making it highly suitable for depicting plant stems and outlines, is called the:
questions.explain: The stem stitch is a basic outline stitch where the thread wraps around itself slightly, creating a twisted, rope-like appearance perfect for embroidering flower stems.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which simple tool is commonly used to hold the fabric tight and flat while executing embroidery stitches?
questions.explain: An embroidery hoop or frame stretches a section of fabric tight like a drum, keeping it smooth and stable so that the needle and thread can pass through evenly.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Where might a student easily source inspiration for beautiful embroidery designs?
options: The dark room of a photo studio.
Nature, flowers, and illustrations in old magazines or gift wrappers.
questions.explain: Nature (leaves, flowers) and printed media (magazines, gift wrappers, and textiles) provide excellent, ready-made visual patterns that can be adapted for embroidery.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: A common method for transferring an embroidery design from a piece of paper directly onto a fabric involves using:
options: Carbon paper and a tracing wheel or pencil
questions.explain: Placing dressmaker's carbon paper between the printed design and the fabric, then tracing over the lines with a pencil or tracing wheel, safely transfers the outline onto the cloth.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Another traditional method of transferring embroidery motifs, which involves poking small holes along the design outline and rubbing colored powder over it, is known as the:
questions.explain: In 'pricking and pouncing', the paper design is perforated (pricked). It is laid on the fabric, and a fine powder (pounce) is rubbed through the holes to recreate the outline.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which embroidery stitch visually consists of a series of linked loops, resembling a metal chain?
questions.explain: The loop stitch, or more commonly the chain stitch, is executed by pulling a loop of thread through the fabric and catching it with the next stitch to form continuous links.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: An embroidery stitch that branches out alternately to the left and right, resembling the barbs of a bird's feather, is called:
questions.explain: The feather stitch is a decorative looping stitch that creates open, branching, tree-like or feather-like lines along the fabric.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: To effectively practice embroidery, which two essential materials are absolutely indispensable?
questions.explain: Embroidery fundamentally requires a needle with an 'eye' large enough to hold thicker strands, and colored embroidery threads or yarns to stitch the designs.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
